html:
SMTO-BOOT-0047 — Your disk is full, so SMTO can't finish starting

GUID: dfa6a7e3-8c6e-4b4f-aaac-cebe2b6fdd1c
Slug: startup-storage-full
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because the disk that holds its data is full, or you've used up your storage allowance on it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Delete files you no longer need, such as old downloads, and empty the trash. Don't delete anything inside SMTO's data folder. SMTO needs free space to finish starting, and its data folder holds your conversations and Tasks.
  2. If you use SMTO on a shared or company computer, ask its administrator to increase your storage allowance. The limit may be your account's allowance rather than the whole disk being full.
  3. Once space is free, select Start again on this screen if you see it, or start SMTO the way you normally do. Starting again only repeats the startup; it doesn't repeat any of your earlier work.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or move SMTO's data folder or its backups to make room.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup failed because the operating system reported no space left on the device or an exceeded disk quota (ENOSPC or EDQUOT) during a required write.

What this means

  • Initialization could not finish a required write because the volume or quota has no available capacity. Removing retained task state is not a safe generic repair.

Why this can happen

  • Initialization could not finish a required write because the volume or quota has no available capacity. Removing retained task state is not a safe generic repair.

How to diagnose it

  • The operating system reported insufficient storage during initialization.
  • The volume has available capacity and restoration completes.

How to fix it

  • Check free space and quota on the volume holding AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR (for example df -h and quota), then free space outside SMTO's runtime state or expand the volume or quota. Keep the state directory and backups intact and restart; do not delete task or conversation state to recover space.
  • Free space outside retained SMTO state or expand the affected volume/quota. Preserve the runtime directory and backups, then restart.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition and run the diagnostic again. Rechecking does not replay tasks or completed operations.

How to verify the fix

  • The volume has available capacity and restoration completes.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
